note: Per-page document ceilings, in IDENTITY (uncompressed) bytes.
HOW THESE WERE SET: from the measured AFTER state of SEO5-09, plus ~10%
headroom. They are not aspirations and not a minimum achievable size.
GOING OVER IS A DECISION, NOT A FAILURE TO BE SILENCED. A page that grows
because it gained something a reader wanted is a page that should have a
bigger number here. Raise it in the SAME commit as the change, and put the
reason in `why`. What this check exists to stop is the other thing: the
homepage grew ~60 KB between the SEO 5.0 audit (821 KB) and Phase 0
(883 KB) with nobody choosing it and nobody noticing.
WHY NOT THE COMPRESSED SIZE. The report prints Brotli and gzip per page,
because that is what a student on a phone downloads. The BUDGET is on the
uncompressed document on purpose: flight payload is extremely repetitive
JSON, so a compressor that gets a little better can shrink the transfer
while the document grows — a compressed ceiling stays green through the
exact regression this file is here to catch.
WHAT IS STILL IN THESE NUMBERS. Card props are no longer the largest
avoidable item. Two known ones remain and are NOT addressed by SEO5-09:
the inline SVG (see `inlineSvgBytes` in the report) and the repeated
next-intl `localeCookie` object. Do not read a green run as 'this is as
small as this page gets'.
Run: npx tsx scripts/measure-page-weight.ts --budget   (needs npm start)
